class.name: PhysXGroom3D
class.description: Draws each strand of a [PhysXGroom] as a thin ribbon turned toward the camera, at least a pixel wide; a strand thinner than a pixel draws that share of it. It's an ordinary mesh to the renderer, so the hair casts and receives shadows and takes the scene's lights like any other, and it shades itself with a hair model (see [member shading_model]) and the groom's baked self-shadowing (see [member self_shadow]). At a distance it draws fewer strands, wider, so the hair keeps its look while it costs less: as many as keep it under about half a strand segment per pixel of its size on screen. [member GeometryInstance3D.lod_bias] keeps more of them (2.0: twice as many), and [member max_strands] caps them. Drawing every strand of a distant groom costs more, not less, than drawing it close up: all of them, a pixel wide each, pile onto the same few pixels. [b]Anti-aliasing:[/b] hair is made of edges thinner than a pixel. MSAA smooths it well; SMAA and FXAA do little for it. [b]Note:[/b] Strands don't move yet: the groom is drawn as imported, in this node's space.

method.name: get_drawn_strand_count
method.description: Returns how many of the groom's strands are drawn now, after the distance and [member max_strands].

members.member: The strands to draw, imported from an Alembic ([code].abc[/code]) file.
The most strands drawn at any distance, 0 for no limit: a quality setting, as games cap grooms at lower settings. The rest of the strands widen to cover the same area.
The hair's color at the root; it blends to [member tip_color] along each strand.
How the strands are drawn. See [enum RenderMode].
How far the highlights spread along the strands: lower is sharper and glossier, higher a softer, wider sheen. Both shading models.

How much light each strand between a point and a light takes away: the light is scaled by [code]exp(-self_shadow)[/code] per strand in its way, as [member PhysXGroom.self_shadow] counted them. It also darkens ambient light inside the hair. 0 turns self-shadowing off; a groom without the bake has none.

How the strands are lit: a choice of look more than of cost. [constant SHADING_MODEL_KAJIYA_KAY] is stylized, bright and saturated with a crisp highlight; [constant SHADING_MODEL_MARSCHNER] is realistic, a softer, more neutral sheen and the glow of backlit hair. With [constant RENDER_MODE_SCREEN_SPACE] they cost the same (drawing the strands is the cost, not lighting them). With [constant RENDER_MODE_MESH], Marschner does more math per light per pixel of hair: on a head filling a 1280×720 view (an RTX 5070), 0.02 ms more GPU time per frame with only the sun, 0.12 ms more with 4 more lights on the hair.
The hair's color at the tip. See [member root_color].
Scales the strands' widths from the groom's: hair drawn a little thicker than real reads fuller, as groomers often do.

constants.constant: A ribbon per strand, turned to face the camera: an ordinary mesh, in every renderer, with every effect that applies to one. Strands thinner than a pixel are dithered, so they need antialiasing (MSAA or TAA) to look smooth. The cheaper mode: on a head filling a 1280×720 view (an RTX 5070), 0.7-1.4 ms of GPU time per frame for 11-29 thousand strands.

The module's own compute passes draw the strands, each with its exact share of every pixel it crosses (as Indiana Jones and the Great Circle does, SIGGRAPH 2025), and the scene's lights and shadows light the two nearest strands in each pixel. Smooth, thin hair with no antialiasing at all, and hair that stays whole when [member width_scale] makes it very thin. Forward+ and Mobile. Costs more close up (1.8-3.0 ms in the view above) and about the same as [constant RENDER_MODE_MESH] at a distance. The mesh still casts the hair's shadows. The hair doesn't write depth, so effects that read the depth buffer don't see it.
Two highlights along each strand, the second tinted by the hair's color (Kajiya and Kay's model). Warm, and holds the hair's color in dark grooms.

Light reflected off each strand, passed through it, and reflected inside it (Marschner's model, with Karis's real-time approximations): physically based, with the glow of backlit hair. Dark hair looks darker and glossier than with [constant SHADING_MODEL_KAJIYA_KAY], as it does in life. See [member shading_model] for what it costs.
